newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia's king to go to Jeddah - source.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia's king to go to Jeddah - source.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's King Fahd is expected to travel from the kingdom's capital Riyadh to the western Red Sea coast city of Jeddah later on Monday, a source close to the Saudi royal family said.
"As far as everyone knows, his majesty will be going to Jeddah within a few hours," he told Reuters.
The source was responding to oil market rumours on Monday that the 75-year-old Saudi monarch, who suffered a stroke in November 1995, had died.
"King Fahd's half-sister died after a long illness on Monday," he added.
The Saudi state-run news agency SPA, quoting a royal court statement, earlier said that Princess Sheikha bint Abdul-Aziz bin Abdul-Rahman al-Saud, 82, died on Monday and would be buried on Tuesday.
King Fahd traditionally spends the last 10 days of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan in holy sites in western Saudi Arabia.
The king had received several Arab officials over the last few days in Riyadh, including Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam on Sunday evening.
